research.topic: Imposter Syndrome – “I’m not really good enough, I’m just faking it”
verified: Imposter syndrome is a persistent self‑doubt and fear of being exposed as a fraud despite evidence of competence.
A substantial proportion of high‑achieving individuals report occasional imposter feelings, and a notable minority experience chronic symptoms, though exact percentages vary across studies.
It is a psychological pattern, not a clinical diagnosis.
Chronic imposter feelings may be associated with reduced motivation and increased burnout, as observed in some high‑pressure fields, though evidence beyond medical education is limited.
Individuals experiencing imposter feelings are often high achievers and may exhibit a strong orientation toward learning, according to some studies.

sources.title: The impostor phenomenon construct in medical education: a meta-analysis of its prevalence and a critical appraisal of its measurement.

research.hook: Myth: ‘If you’re feeling like a fraud, you just need to work harder.’ Fact: Your brain is actually playing tricks on you – and no amount of extra hours will fix it.
research.tip: Keep an “Evidence Log” – write one concrete achievement after each task and review it weekly to counter the fraud narrative.

data.title_en: When you feel like a fraud, watch this video

scenes.text: Kya aapko lagta hai aap fraud ho?
scenes.text_en: Do you feel like you are a fraud?

scenes.text: Fact ye hai ki tumhara brain tricks play kar raha hai, aur ek simple solution aapko aage batayenge.
scenes.text_en: The fact is your brain plays tricks, and we’ll reveal a simple solution soon.

scenes.text: Ye self‑doubt persistent hota hai, chahe evidence ho ki tum competent ho.
scenes.text_en: This self‑doubt persists even when evidence shows you are competent.

scenes.text: Bade high‑achievers bhi aksar aisi feelings experience karte hain.
scenes.text_en: Many high‑achieving individuals often experience these feelings.

scenes.text: Ye koi clinical diagnosis nahi, bas ek psychological pattern hai.
scenes.text_en: It is not a clinical diagnosis, just a psychological pattern.

scenes.text: Aise feelings ke baare mein kisi trusted dost ya counselor se baat karna madadgar ho sakta hai.
scenes.text_en: Talking about these feelings with a trusted friend or counselor can help.

scenes.text: Ek engineering student, jo project deadline se pressure mein hai, aksar sochta hai ki woh qualify nahi hai.
scenes.text_en: An engineering student under project deadline pressure often feels unqualified.

scenes.text: Ek junior manager, meeting mein ideas rakhte hue, darrta hai ki sab usko fraud samjhenge.
scenes.text_en: A junior manager presenting ideas fears everyone will think they’re a fraud.

scenes.text: High‑pressure fields mein chronic feelings burnout aur motivation kam kar sakti hain, lekin aise log learning ke liye strong orientation rakhte hain.
scenes.text_en: In high‑pressure fields chronic feelings can cause burnout and lower motivation, yet such people often have a strong learning orientation.

scenes.text: Is fraud narrative ko har week counter karne ka ek simple tarika hai.
scenes.text_en: There is a simple weekly method to counter this fraud narrative.

scenes.text: Ek Evidence Log banao aur har task ke baad apni achievement likho.
scenes.text_en: Create an Evidence Log and write your achievement after each task.

scenes.text: Jab bhi lage ki tum faking ho, apna evidence log weekly check karo.
scenes.text_en: Whenever you feel you’re faking it, review your evidence log weekly.

data.description: Understand why high-achieving students and professionals feel like frauds and learn how an evidence log helps counter self-doubt.
